topic: Look 4 · Unit 2: Move to the Music! — Lesson 5 (Song) & Lesson 7 (Video) · SB 22, 24 · WB 19 · Grade 4 (periods 8–9)
title: World Music Academy
subtitle: Play it loudly, play it softly — but never play it wrong 🎶

features.title: A Song You Can Sing
features.desc: Adverbs are hiding in the lyrics. Find them once and the rule is yours.

features.title: A Video, Six Countries
features.desc: Vietnam to India — six instruments, and how each one is actually played.

features.title: Three Games
features.desc: Scramble the words, match country to instrument, sort adverb from adjective.

features.title: One Rule That Lasts
features.desc: adjective + ly = adverb. It answers one question: how? Play it and keep it.

method.phase: Vocab → Game → Review (the lesson is the clickable core of the unit-2 session)

games.name: Word Scramble
games.why: production under a clock — the hint is the meaning, so the word is retrieved, not copied

games.name: Country & Instrument Match
games.why: paired recall — country and instrument are stored as one chunk, which is how the video teaches them

games.name: Adverb or Adjective Sort
games.why: metacognitive sorting — the learner has to name the question each word answers, which is the rule itself

voice: Say it LOUD. Say it WRONG. But SAY IT.
The word a student learns while winning a game will still be in their mouth ten years from now.

storyline: Linh and Nam talk after the school concert, then in the group chat about the instruments from the Unit 2 video. The lesson runs in two periods: the song first, the video second, with the games and the test closing it.

rooms.title: The Entrance
rooms.label: Warm-Up
rooms.content:
Two periods, one concert 🎶 Period 8 is the song; period 9 is the video. By the end you can say how something is done — and you will know six instruments by the country they come from.

  • Eight words: four adverbs and four music words
  • The rule that turns loud into loudly
  • A song you sing and a video you watch — with the adverbs hiding inside them
  • Six countries, six traditional instruments, and one adverb you will act out

rooms.title: The School Concert
rooms.label: Scene
rooms.content:
Linh: Did you hear Mai play the violin last night? She played so beautifully 🎻
Nam: I did! And the drums behind her — Tuan banged them loudly. I could feel it in my chair.
Linh: He was supposed to play softly in the second part. He didn't.
Nam: He was too excited. He hit the drums with one stick and then he dropped it 😄
Linh: Nobody minded. Everybody clapped quickly — like they wanted more.
🤔 Reality check: beautifully, loudly, softly, quickly — none of them name a thing. They all answer one question: how did it happen?

rooms.title: The Group Chat
rooms.label: Text Scene
rooms.content:
Nam: guys the video in class today — that long wooden pipe 🙄
Linh: the didgeridoo! Australia. You play it with your lips, not your hands 😏
Nam: and Scotland has the bagpipes. They play them LOUDLY at parades 🎺
Linh: Vietnam has the đàn bầu — one string, and you bend the note softly until it sings 🪕
Nam: our teacher played one chord on the piano and the whole class went quiet 😅
🤔 Reality check: every country has an instrument that sounds like home. Learning the country and the instrument together is how you remember both.
Pro Tip: adjective + -ly = adverb. loud → loudly · soft → softly · beautiful → beautifully · quick → quickly. It tells you how someone does something: She plays the guitar beautifully.

rooms.title: The Words
rooms.label: Learn
rooms.content:
1. quickly: fast, with speed — She played the fast part quickly.
2. softly: with very little sound — He hummed softly so nobody heard.
3. loudly: with a lot of sound — They played the bagpipes loudly.
4. beautifully: in a lovely way — Mai played the violin beautifully.
5. chord: two or more notes played together, at the same time.
6. stick: the thin wooden thing a drummer hits the drums with — a drumstick.
7. traditional: belonging to a country's old culture, handed down for years — a traditional instrument.
8. popular: liked by a lot of people — pop music is short for popular music.
The rule in one line: adjective + ly = adverb. loud → loudly. And the adverb answers HOW? — Tuan banged the drums loudly. Not loud. Never loud.

rooms.title: The Song — How Do You Play It?
rooms.label: Song
rooms.content:
How to use this room: read the chant out loud with a clap on the strong beat — it is built so the adverb lands on the beat. Sing it twice: once for the words, once to hunt the adverbs.

🎵 How Do You Play It? (a class chant — clap on the strong beat)

I play the drums — I play them loudly.
I play the flute — I play it softly.
I play the violin — beautifully.
How do you play it? Tell me how!

The sitar sings so softly,
the bagpipes call so loudly,
the castanets go click-click quickly —
how do you play it? Tell me how!

One chord, then two, then three,
one stick for the drum and me.
Is it traditional? Is it popular?
Play it once and you will see.

Lyric hunt: in the first verse, which word tells you HOW the drums are played?
Lyric hunt: the chant says the castanets go click-click quickly. What kind of word is quickly?
🤔 Reality check: every verse hides its adverb, and every adverb answers the same question — HOW? Take the adverbs out and you still know what happens, but not how it happened.
Act it out: pick one adverb from the chant and mime it for your partner — bang, hum, or click. They have to say it back in a full sentence: “You played it loudly.”

rooms.title: The Video — Around the World in Six Instruments
rooms.label: Video
rooms.content:
Watch for: the video names six countries and one instrument each — and it always says how the instrument is played. Read the transcript once for the countries, then again for the adverbs.

📺 Around the World in Six Instruments (video transcript)

Every country keeps one instrument that sounds like home.

In Vietnam, the đàn bầu has one string and a thin bamboo stick. The player bends the note softly until it sings.

In Scotland, the bagpipes are played loudly at parades. You hear them before you see them.

In Australia, the didgeridoo is a long wooden pipe. You play it with your lips, and it sounds like the wind.

In Japan, the taiko drums are hit hard with big sticks. In Spain, dancers click castanets quickly in their hands. In India, the sitar has many strings and a soft, bright sound.

Some of these are traditional instruments — they belong to an old culture and have been handed down for years. Others, like the guitar, are popular all over the world today.

Circle the correct answer: according to the video, which instrument is played loudly at parades?
Circle the correct answer: the sitar comes from India. How does the video describe its sound?
🤔 Reality check: swap the adverbs round and the video breaks — nobody plays the bagpipes softly at a parade. The adverb is not decoration; it carries the meaning.

rooms.title: The Definitions — From Memory
rooms.label: Definitions
rooms.content:
No looking back: the transcript is behind you. Answer from memory — that is the whole point of this room. If you miss, you are allowed to walk back one room and read it again.
Complete the definition: a _____ is the thin wooden thing a drummer hits the drums with.
Complete the definition: two or more notes played together, at the same time, make a _____.
Now say it your way: give your partner a definition of traditional and popular without using the words. If they guess both, you have the vocabulary.

rooms.title: Game 1 — Word Scramble
rooms.label: Game 1
rooms.content: How to win: the hint under each row is the meaning — read it, then click the tiles in order. A wrong word shakes and clears itself, so nothing is lost.

rooms.title: Game 2 — Country & Instrument
rooms.label: Game 2
rooms.content: How to win: click a country on the left, then its instrument on the right. Six pairs. Wrong pairs shake and let go — guess boldly.

rooms.title: Game 3 — Adverb or Adjective?
rooms.label: Game 3
rooms.content: How to win: click a word, then the group it belongs to. Remember the two questions — HOW? is the adverb, WHAT KIND? is the adjective.

rooms.title: The Test
rooms.label: Test
rooms.content:
Scenario: Mai played the violin _____. Everybody stopped to listen.
Scenario: You hear the music loudly before you see the band. There are parades and bagpipes. Where are you?
Scenario: “Tuan banged the drums loudly.” Which word tells you HOW he banged them?

rooms.title: The Key
rooms.label: Mastery
rooms.content:
🎓 You now hold the key
  • adjective + ly = adverb: loud → loudly · soft → softly · beautiful → beautifully · quick → quickly.
  • Adverbs say HOW: Tuan banged the drums loudly. He should have played softly.
  • Six countries, six instruments: Vietnam – đàn bầu · Scotland – bagpipes · Australia – didgeridoo · Japan – taiko drums · Spain – castanets · India – sitar.
  • Music words: chord (notes played together) · stick (a drumstick) · traditional (old, handed down) · popular (liked by many).
  • Read for the adverb: the song and the video both say how, not just what — swap the adverbs and the meaning breaks.
Level Up: tonight, play or hear one piece of music and say two sentences about it out loud — what the instrument is, and how it is played. Then ask your partner about theirs: “How do you play it?” That is the pair discussion, done for real.
Write it down (WB page 19): two sentences about an instrument you know — what it is, and how it is played. Use one adverb from the song.
